what_it_does: Understanding what a chip design does — and predicting how it will behave — is valuable for automated chip design tools. Two types of AI models are useful here: large language models (the same kind that power chatbots) that read the high-level human-written chip description and understand its intent, and graph neural networks (AI that reasons about connected structures, like circuit wires) that understand the low-level gate-by-gate wiring diagram. MOSS combines both: it uses a language model to enrich the representation of memory-storing elements (called flip-flops, the basic building blocks that hold a circuit's state from one clock tick to the next), and a graph model that avoids getting overwhelmed by very long chains of connected gates. The two models supervise each other during training, and the combined representation outperforms either alone.
